42853992.text: A 72-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for restaging due to significantly increased PSA levels during chemotherapy. Imaging revealed high 68Ga-PSMA-11 uptake in bilateral adrenal uptake, with additional uptake in the prostate and few sclerotic bone lesions. MRI and afterwards adrenal gland biopsy confirmed adrenal metastases, an uncommon metastatic site. As the patient was oligometastatic, refractory to previous systemic therapies, and ineligible for surgery or radiotherapy, 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy was initiated. After four treatment cycles, PSA levels progressively decreased, and post-therapeutic follow-up SPECT/CT demonstrated a near-complete response in adrenal and bone metastases without treatment-related adverse effects.

42912542.text: A 2-year-old girl was diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma. Baseline 18F-MFBG PET/CT demonstrated primary abdominal disease with concurrent multiple metastases. Following induction therapy, restaging 18F-MFBG PET/CT did not show any abnormal 18F-MFBG uptake. However, at six-month follow-up, repeat 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed multifocal 18F-MFBG-avid lesions confined exclusively to the cranial compartment, with no evidence of extracranial disease recurrence. Subsequent contrast-enhanced brain MRI confirmed the presence of leptomeningeal metastases. This case illustrates that isolated multifocal leptomeningeal metastases may be reliably detected on 18F-MFBG PET/CT, underscoring the utility of this modality in the surveillance of central nervous system involvement in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma.

42912642.text: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18 F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18 F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18 F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68 Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

42925842.label: Objectives
42925842.text: Despite the recent introduction of O-RADS MRI to standardize MRI assessment of adnexal lesions, diagnostic imaging remains challenging. Artificial intelligence might provide help in radiological decision support. Therefore, we trained deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) for detection and classification of benign and malignant adnexal lesions.

42925842.label: Materials and methods
42925842.text: Two radiologists (R1/R2) retrospectively assigned MR-O-RADS scores on multiparametric MRI performed in 144 patients (median age 50.2 ± 14.3 years) prospectively included between 11/2016-12/2024 after diagnosis of indeterminate adnexal lesions on transvaginal ultrasound. R1 manually three-dimensionally segmented ovaries/adnexal lesions. Histopathology or 2-year-follow-up served as gold standard. Transverse T2WI, T1WI, T1WI fat-saturated, T1WI post-contrast, DWI and ADC maps were used for further analysis. nnU-Net was trained in 5-fold-cross-validation using three designs: D1) T2WI only at full resolution, D2) all 6 sequences at full resolution, D3) T2WI only downsampled by half in-plane. Prediction performance and specificity of malignant vs. benign entities was evaluated using ROC-AUC methods and the McNemar test for clustered data.

42925842.label: Results
42925842.text: The dataset included annotations of 237 ovaries (130 benign and 67 malignant histopathologies, 40 lesions with negative 2-year-follow-up). R1/R2/D1/D2/D3 models achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.96/0.96/0.86/0.86/0.84 (95%CI 0.93-1.00/0.93-1.00/0.81-0.92/0.78-0.93/0.77-0.91), respectively. Cluster-adjusted AUC of R1/2 was significantly higher than D1-D3 models (all p < 0.001). Youden index specificity/sensitivity was 0.95/0.91,0.94/0.93,0.88/0.73,0.90/0.76,0.87/0.76, while it was 0.95/0.91,0.48/0.91,0.39/0.91,0.42/0.91 at the closest operating point to sensitivity ≥ 90%, with specificity of R1/2 being significantly higher than D1-3 models (all p < 0.001). Subanalysis in cases with full agreement between all CNN models demonstrated similar relationships. Subset analysis in frequent histopathologies showed AUCs of 1.0/0.99 (95%CI 1.00-1.00/0.98-1.00) for radiologists and 0.98 (95%CI 0.96-1.00) for model D2.

42925842.label: Conclusions
42925842.text: Deep learning models achieved overall validation set performance at AUC ≥ 0.84, lower than the radiologists, however in frequent histopathologies D2 achieved AUC = 0.98, not statistically different from R1/2, suggesting that training with more examples especially of infrequent histopathologies may further increase performance.

42945842.label: Objective
42945842.text: To assess the intra- and inter-reader reliability of measurements of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions on serial multiparametric MRI scans, and to assess how lesion characteristics and measurement methods influence measurements over time in an international two-centre setting.

42945842.label: Materials and methods
42945842.text: Twenty patients with low- or intermediate-risk PCa undergoing active surveillance were included. A total of three MRI scans were evaluated for each patient: one baseline and two serial follow-up scans. Five consultant radiologists from two institutions independently measured the size of the index lesion at each time point by four methods: maximum diameter, biaxial diameters, ellipsoid volume, and planimetry. Measurements were repeated after a four-week 'wash-out' period. Variability was assessed using strip plots and Bland-Altman analysis.

42945842.label: Results
42945842.text: Graphical presentation of inter-reader and intra-reader reliability enabled examination of variability between methods, readers and reads. Variability increased with lesion size and was greatest for lesions with poorly defined margins. Smaller, well-delineated lesions demonstrated greater consistency over time and across readers. Estimates of percentage change showed greater variability than absolute measurements, particularly for volumetric methods. Small differences in the underlying absolute measurements are amplified when expressed relative to baseline values.

42945842.label: Conclusion
42945842.text: Serial MRI assessment of PCa lesion size is subject to substantial variability, particularly for larger lesions and lesions with indistinct boundaries. The benefits of consistent readers and measurement methods warrant further confirmation in larger prospective studies to support reliable clinical decision-making during active surveillance.

42961642.label: Objective
42961642.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of spectral CT-derived quantitative parameters for preoperative prediction of pathologic grade in urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (UCB) and to assess their incremental value over clinical variables and model robustness.

42961642.label: Methods
42961642.text: In this retrospective study, patients with pathologically confirmed UCB who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced spectral CT were included. Quantitative spectral parameters were extracted. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Variables with P < 0.10 on univariable analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression to construct clinical, imaging and combined models. Model robustness was evaluated using penalized regression (LASSO and elastic net) as sensitivity analyses. Model performance and clinical net benefit were assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, DeLong testing, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

42961642.label: Results
42961642.text: A total of 120 patients were included (65 high-grade tumours and 55 low-grade tumours). Spectral parameters showed good to excellent inter-reader agreement. Several imaging features were associated with tumor grade on univariable analysis (P < 0.05). After inclusion of calcification in the clinical analysis, age remained independently associated with tumor grade, whereas tumor size, tumor number, and calcification were not statistically significant in the multivariable clinical model. AEF remained the only independent imaging predictor. The AUC was 0.743 for the imaging model, 0.746 for the clinical model and 0.772 for the combined model. The incremental improvement of the combined model over the clinical model was small (ΔAUC = 0.027) and not statistically significant (DeLong P = 0.563). DCA showed limited additional net benefit of the combined model at intermediate risk thresholds.

42961642.label: Conclusion
42961642.text: Spectral CT-derived parameters are associated with pathologic grade in UCB but demonstrate only moderate discriminatory performance.

42965692.text: Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) is a high-resolution 3D gradient-echo (GRE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique that combines magnitude and phase information to increase sensitivity to blood products, iron, calcification, thrombus, and venous structures. In routine practice, SWI should be interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, processed SWI images, and minimum-intensity projection (minIP) images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-dependent phase conventions. Its most established role is in brain MRI, particularly in: suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy; baseline and follow-up assessment of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with haemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H) during anti-amyloid therapy; traumatic brain injury; multiple sclerosis work-up, when assessment of the central vein sign or paramagnetic rim lesions is clinically relevant; neuro-oncology; and vascular malformations. Overall, these constitute the core recommended brain scenarios for SWI supported by moderate to high levels of evidence. Outside neuroradiology (e.g., musculoskeletal, abdominal, breast, pelvic, and cardiac imaging), SWI remains promising but less standardised and should currently be reserved for selected problem-solving indications. KEY POINTS: SWI should be acquired as a high-resolution 3D GRE sequence and interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, and post-processed minIP images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-specific phase conventions. SWI should be included in brain MRI protocols when haemorrhagic or microvascular susceptibility findings are expected to affect diagnosis or management, especially in cerebral amyloid angiopathy, anti-amyloid therapy monitoring, traumatic brain injury, and neuro-oncology or multiple sclerosis work-up. Outside neuroradiology, SWI can be used as a targeted problem-solving adjunct rather than as a routine sequence.

42975642.label: Purpose
42975642.text: Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index.

42975642.label: Methods
42975642.text: We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites.

42975642.label: Results
42975642.text: Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05.

42975642.label: Conclusion
42975642.text: The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

42975842.label: Objectives
42975842.text: To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).

42975842.label: Materials and methods
42975842.text: This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images.

42975842.label: Results
42975842.text: Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%).

42975842.label: Conclusion
42975842.text: The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure.

42975842.label: Key points
42975842.text: Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

42986492.label: Objective
42986492.text: To evaluate the performance of the deep progressive reconstruction method (DPR) for low-dose 18F-FDG PET imaging in pediatric patients.

42986492.label: Methods
42986492.text: Forty-one pediatric patients who underwent clinical 18F-FDG PET/CT were retrospectively enrolled. List-mode PET data acquired at 2 min per bed position were reconstructed using OSEM and DPR, generating the standard-dose images labelled OSEM_full and DPR_full, respectively. To simulate low-dose conditions, the acquisition time of the original list-mode data was reduced to 1/n (n = 2, 3, 4) and reconstructed with DPR, yielding DPR_1/2, DPR_1/3, and DPR_1/4. For all reconstruction groups, quantitative metrics including the standard uptake value (SUV) and coefficient of variation (COV) in the liver, blood pool, and gluteus maximus, as well as lesion tumour-to-background ratio (TBR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Subjective image quality was evaluated based on overall image quality, lesion conspicuity, and image noise. Age-stratified subgroup analysis was performed, with OSEM_full as the reference standard.

42986492.label: Results
42986492.text: DPR reconstructions showed good agreement in quantitative accuracy with reference imaging. Compared with OSEM_full, DPR_full and DPR_1/2 significantly lowered background COV, DPR_1/3 showed comparable background noise, while DPR_1/4 presented increased noise. All DPR groups yielded significantly higher lesion TBR, and DPR_full, DPR_1/2, DPR_1/3 improved lesion CNR, whereas DPR_1/4 showed reduced CNR. Subjectively, DPR_full and DPR_1/2 achieved significantly higher image quality scores, with over 60% of cases rated as excellent. Age subgroup analysis revealed that DPR_1/3 performance was age-dependent, with better noise control and higher CNR in older children but poorer performance in younger children, suggesting its suitability as an age-adaptive dose reduction strategy. Notably, all DPR protocols improved lesion TBR across all age groups.

42986492.label: Conclusion
42986492.text: DPR enables substantial dose reduction in pediatric ¹⁸F-FDG PET while maintaining or even improving objective and subjective image quality. Among the dose-reduction protocols, DPR_1/2 provides the best overall performance, while DPR_1/3 represents the optimal balance between dose reduction and image quality, particularly in older children. These findings support the clinical potential for personalised low-dose PET strategies in the pediatric population.

43049892.label: Objectives
43049892.text: To evaluate whether CT-derived radiomics and deep learning features can improve non-invasive risk stratification of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk gastroesophageal varices (HRVs) in cirrhotic patients.

43049892.label: Materials and methods
43049892.text: This retrospective study included 454 cirrhotic patients from center A and 77 from center B. CSPH labels were available only for patients from center A. Patients in both centers with available endoscopic findings were classified as HRVs or non-HRVs. A dual-path modeling framework integrating radiomics and deep learning-derived features extracted from multiple major hepatic vessels was developed, and was compared with single-path (radiomics-only and deep learning-only), single-vessel, vascular geometric, and clinical-feature-based models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

43049892.label: Results
43049892.text: For CSPH prediction, the dual-path model achieved the highest AUC (0.892 vs. 0.678-0.870 for the other models; P < 0.05 for most comparisons). For HRVs prediction, the proposed model achieved AUCs of 0.790 and 0.782 in the internal and external test set, respectively. The proposed model consistently outperformed the single-path models (0.625-0.648; all P < 0.05), single-vessel models (0.526-0.642; all P < 0.05), the vascular geometric model (0.528; P < 0.01), and the clinical-feature-based models (0.327-0.728; P < 0.001 for the APRI-based model) in the external test set.

43049892.label: Conclusion
43049892.text: A dual-path model integrating multi-vessel radiomics and deep learning features demonstrates robust predictive performance for CSPH and HRVs in cirrhotic patients. This approach may provide a new non-invasive alternative for risk stratification and clinical management of portal hypertension-related complications.

43071592.text: Immunoglobulin G4-related hypertrophic pachymeningitis (IgG4-RHP) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder with high biopsy risk. A 58-year-old man had a 2-year history of persistent headache. Brain MRI revealed craniocervical dural thickening. Dual-tracer ¹⁸F-FDG and ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT were performed. Compared with ¹⁸F-FDG, ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed higher radiotracer uptake intensity and sharper lesion demarcation, and additionally uncovered occult inflammatory lesions that were invisible on ¹⁸F-FDG imaging. Elevated serum IgG4 confirmed the diagnosis, which fulfilled the 2019 ACR/EULAR IgG4-RD criteria. For patients unsuitable for biopsy, ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT offers unique diagnostic advantages for this rare disease.
